Trust expiry uses clock_timestamp() in a fresh statement after lock acquisition, not transaction-start NOW(). Lock order is user, sessions, trust, matching successful OTP completion. review: One UUID wallet per profile; int8 posted/reserved defaults, version and timestamp. Available balance is derived. Ledger has UUIDv7 identity, wallet FK, constrained types/states, nonzero signed amounts, unique idempotency, references, metadata and timestamps. Production constraints prevent negative posted/reserved/available balances; no stored available column.

Credit, debit and reserve lock profile then wallet, bind the canonical UUID and validate exact command replay. Different wallet/type/amount/ref/state collisions reject. New writes reject archived profiles. Credit atomically inserts Completed ledger and increments posted/version with the required nonnegative predicate. Debit reserves then completes inside one transaction; insufficient available balance leaves no debit. Reserve/release update only held funds; release is idempotent and preserves ledger history.

Optimistic delta requires the expected version and increments it atomically; stale/missing rows fail. Production callers are credit/reversal transaction owners. Existing integration cases cover same-key and distinct-key races, overdraw/overreserve prevention, canonical UUIDs and rollback. Original completed reversal rows remain in the ledger with a compensating row, consistent with reconciliation aggregation.

Reconciliation runs through the guarded scheduled poller, compares Completed and Reserved sums, locks/rechecks candidates, records exact deltas in the finance exception queue and suppresses duplicate unresolved exceptions. It never rewrites balances. Six unsafe numeric-to-int8 SUM casts could abort the candidate query;48ac9d7 removes them. Three real production-schema cases prove positive posted, positive reserved and negative posted overflow are reported alongside ordinary mismatches, with exact values and no duplicate or money mutation.

Dashboard/wallet reads enforce current owner/agent permissions and return exact decimal-string money. Low-balance warning compares available funds with due unpaid invoice liabilities, excluding unrelated/future invoices.
